---
title: "Optimizer Graph Container: stages-as-data over the existing engine (jtml-production PoC)"
type: refactor
status: active
date: 2026-08-12
origin: docs/brainstorms/2026-08-12-optimizer-path-requirements.md
---

# Optimizer Graph Container: stages-as-data over the existing engine

## Overview

JTML's optimizer run shape is hard-coded in `OptimizerManager::Optimize()`
(trunk 20k → 2×branch 5k → leaf 5k, cumulative 20/25/30/35k, dilation 6/4/1).
This plan makes that shape **data**: a StageScript (a vector of StageSpec)
built by pure functions, executed by the existing `Optimize()` loop through
the existing seams — driver, `RunDirectStage`, GPU cost path, IoU gates —
with **bit-identical behavior** as the feasibility PoC (requirement R6–R7).

The plan executes Phases 0–2 of the confirmed research-run path
(origin R8): the foundation that makes the baseline trustworthy (bug pins,
behavior-neutral fixes, the live distance-map index fix, exactly one
re-baseline, the CUDA-free finite-check), the two measurement instruments
that pin the container (z-profile probe, multi-stage oracle), and the
container itself (Cuts A/B/C/F → the `jtml-production` graph). The algorithm
battery, the CUDA/perf workstream (incl. Cut 0 instrumentation + Cut 4 meter
fix, origin R10), and the polish horizon are **separate follow-up plans** —
per the session decision to keep the graph work independent of CUDA work.

Normative grounding: `.panoptes/optimizer-deep-dive/synthesis.org` (angle 04
= backend architecture; findings 1–14) — every gate, pin, and line reference
below comes from it or from the verification pass this plan's research ran
against the current tree.

---

## Problem Frame

The run shape is code, not data: `Optimize()`'s stage loop
(`src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp`) interleaves session/GPU state and
signal emission with the only algorithm policy — the trunk/branch/leaf
sequence. Changing any per-stage constant (budget, range, dilation, variant,
ordering) is an edit to a 1,700-line QObject manager, and the search is
currently measured against a baseline contaminated by one live kernel bug
(`distance_map_metric.cu:27` grid-index formula, verified). The owner's goal:
express runs as **graphs** (configurations, not code edits), prove the
container works bit-identically over the existing engine, and only then
improve the optimization itself.

The current shape, expressed as the v1 graph (verified against the code and
`test/golden/baseline.json`):

```
jtml-production:  [Trunk: classic DIRECT, budget 20000, range (35)^6, dil 6]
               -> [Branch x2: classic DIRECT, budget 5000 each, range (15,15,25,25,25,25), dil 4]
               -> [Leaf: classic DIRECT, budget 5000, range (3,3,15,3,3,3), dil 1]
cumulative caps: 20000 / 25000 / 30000 / 35000
```

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1 (graph = ordered stages, implicit seed-forwarding edges): U7, U9
- R2 (C++-typed named registry; manifest references by name): U7
- R3 (per-stage optimizer-variant slot, bit-identical classic default): U8
- R4 (execute through existing seams; no new layer; Cut E deferred): U7, U9
- R5 (schema must not preclude biplane / tiered-dilation / polish): U7
- R6 (v1 registry ships `jtml-production`; stubs allowed): U7, U9
- R7 (behavior-preserving PoC: caps, bookkeeping, poses, oracle green, qml
  parity; four lineage invariants asserted): U4, U6, U9
- R8 (sequencing confirmed: this plan executes Phases 0–2): U1–U10
- R9 (no algorithm delta before the apparatus): honored — no variant work in
  this plan; the battery is a follow-up plan
- R10 (Cut 0 + Cut 4 early): **deferred to the follow-up perf plan** (see
  Scope Boundaries — session decision to keep CUDA work separate; this
  plan's gates are oracle-IoU + bit-identity, not measured evals/s)

**Origin actors:** A1 (owner — registers graphs), A2 (measurement harness —
scores), A3 (production app — consumes the default graph unchanged)
**Origin flows:** F1 (graph-driven optimizer run), F2 (harness scoring)
**Origin acceptance examples:** AE1 (multi-stage oracle drives
`jtml-production` through the driver seam; costCalls on 20/25/30/35k; four
lineage invariants hold; per-frame IoU ≥ 0.85 vs the re-baselined values)

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No algorithm work: no variant switch, no battery, no `1-DTC-GL-gb` (R9).
  The per-stage variant slot is built (U8) and stays at bit-identical
  defaults.
- No CUDA/perf work: no Cut 0 instrumentation, no Cut 4 meter fix, no async
  copies, no N-way batching, no batch seam (origin R10–R14 → the follow-up
  perf plan, which also owns the meter's 1000× unit-error fix).
- No polish work: no four-arm study, no simplex arm, no G1–G4 gate (origin
  R16 → horizon plan).
- No measurement expansion beyond the pinning instruments: the ablation
  runner + `ablation.json` + perturbation suite are the follow-up
  measurement plan (origin R9's scoring surface is only *prepared* here via
  the probe + multi-stage oracle).
- No re-litigation of the run's resolved decisions (Mahfouz normalization
  kernel-as-spec; dilation three-way as ablation axis; gb numbers; GLh
  formula; NaN-impossibility of DIRECT_DILATION).
- No caching/memoization (origin R14), no biplane, no ML initializer beyond
  a schema note (origin R5/R15/R16).

### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- **Perf plan (CUDA workstream)**: Cut 0 instrumentation, Cut 4 meter fix,
  Cut 1 async copies, streamed N-way + batch seam + N-bank eval state, all
  parked perf items (fragment-fill removal, metric fusion, resolution arm,
  pose-array design) — gated on the re-baseline this plan produces.
- **Measurement plan**: ablation runner + `ablation.json` + perturbation
  suite, bench-marks block, ci/nightly profiles.
- **Algorithm plan**: analytic battery, staged basin-capture metric, variant
  switch (needs this plan's harness).
- **Hygiene pass (run's Phase-3 items)**: Mahfouz value guards
  (`implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/:446`), curvature de-scope
  (`DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:42-43`), dilation doc reconciliation to measured
  values, ON-vs-OFF silhouette IoU protocol. Kept out of this plan to keep
  the container work focused; the re-baseline stays single-variable either
  way.
- **Polish horizon plan**: four-arm study, Yamazaki z-arm, biplane, ML
  initializer.

---

## Context & Research

### Relevant Code and Patterns

- `src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp` — the `Optimize()` stage loop
  (landmarks: trunk reset :995–996, branch group single init/dilate/emit
  :1052–1076 before the repeat loop :1080, `budget_ +=` :1096/:1151,
  `CalculateSymTrap` :1135, leaf error-gated destruct :1158–1163, epilogue
  trunk-restore :1170–1184), `RunDirectStage` + injected-cost lambda
  (:1234–1252), `EvaluateCostFunctionAtPoint` (:1372–1387), the manager's
  per-manager parameter scan (dilation/dark-silhouette, :237–345).
- `include/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.h` + `src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp` —
  the by-value `OptimizerRunLaunch` seam; adapter forwards verbatim
  (:58–78); sole `new OptimizerManager` at :31.
- `include/domain/direct_optimizer.h` + `src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp` —
  the extracted DIRECT: injected `std::function<double(const Point6D&)>`
  cost, cumulative guard `(calls + offset) < budget_`, `SetCallOffset`,
  callbacks, largest-denormalized-side one-side trisection. Note the stale
  illustrative comment at direct_optimizer.h:19–20 ("trunk 10k → branch 20k
  → leaf 30k") — fix opportunistically in U8.
- `include/coordinator/optimizer_run_controller_core.h` — typed `Directive`
  enum incl. `SymTrap=5` (:64–69); the counter-derived observation channel
  (stageText/costCalls/progress) the oracle's stage-bookkeeping gate uses.
- The named-registry pattern to mirror: `CostFunctionManager`'s
  `listCostFunctions()` (CostFunctionManager.cpp:343+) — C++-typed named
  data — and its services-layer sibling `BuildCostFunctionRegistryEntries`
  (`src/services/cost_function_registry.cpp`, golden-pinned).
- `test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp` — the GPU Tier-2 oracle; the hand-rolled
  cost twin at :286–291 (monoplane-only; `kBudget=3000` flat shape; Canny
  3/0/150 pinned; IoU/L1 gate vs the Study2Grid label).
- `test/golden/baseline.json` — canonical caps [20000, 25000, 30000, 35000];
  the re-baseline event's target.
- CMake conventions — `src/coordinator/CMakeLists.txt` uses an explicit
  .cpp source list + header GLOB: new `optimizer_stage_script.cpp` needs one
  added line; test targets follow the direct-compile pattern (see
  Institutional Learnings).

### Institutional Learnings

- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-testability-and-cmake-conventions-2026-08-07.md` —
  the master playbook: cumulative budget 20/25/30/35k is **load-bearing** (do
  NOT "fix" to per-stage caps); direct-compile test pattern; AUTOMOC gotcha
  (Q_OBJECT headers in the test target's source list); oracle/baseline.json
  contract; Tier-1 golden + hegel PBT twin house rule.
- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-layered-lib-split-2026-08-08.md` —
  layered-lib conventions; new .cpp files must be added to the explicit
  source list; attesting zero behavior change for pure relocation.
- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-shared-vm-layer-2026-08-11.md` — the
  shared-layer map: `OptimizerRunController`/core (epoch gate, stage math),
  driver seam, relay channel; the multi-stage oracle is the seam's next
  consumer.
- `docs/solutions/logic-errors/cost-function-parameter-double-truncation-2026-08-08.md` —
  typed cost parameters: hegel PBT invariants catch type-class bugs in the
  parameter registry (relevant to U1's metric-semantics PBT twins).

# Optimizer Graph Container: stages-as-data over the existing engine

## Overview

JTML's optimizer run shape is hard-coded in `OptimizerManager::Optimize()`
(trunk 20k → 2×branch 5k → leaf 5k, cumulative 20/25/30/35k, dilation 6/4/1).
This plan makes that shape **data**: a StageScript (a vector of StageSpec)
built by pure functions, executed by the existing `Optimize()` loop through
the existing seams — driver, `RunDirectStage`, GPU cost path, IoU gates —
with **bit-identical behavior** as the feasibility PoC (requirement R6–R7).

The plan executes Phases 0–2 of the confirmed research-run path
(origin R8): the foundation that makes the baseline trustworthy (bug pins,
behavior-neutral fixes, the live distance-map index fix, exactly one
re-baseline, the CUDA-free finite-check), the two measurement instruments
that pin the container (z-profile probe, multi-stage oracle), and the
container itself (Cuts A/B/C/F → the `jtml-production` graph). The algorithm
battery, the CUDA/perf workstream (incl. Cut 0 instrumentation + Cut 4 meter
fix, origin R10), and the polish horizon are **separate follow-up plans** —
per the session decision to keep the graph work independent of CUDA work.

Normative grounding: `.panoptes/optimizer-deep-dive/synthesis.org` (angle 04
= backend architecture; findings 1–14) — every gate, pin, and line reference
below comes from it or from the verification pass this plan's research ran
against the current tree.

---

## Problem Frame

The run shape is code, not data: `Optimize()`'s stage loop
(`src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp`) interleaves session/GPU state and
signal emission with the only algorithm policy — the trunk/branch/leaf
sequence. Changing any per-stage constant (budget, range, dilation, variant,
ordering) is an edit to a 1,700-line QObject manager, and the search is
currently measured against a baseline contaminated by one live kernel bug
(`distance_map_metric.cu:27` grid-index formula, verified). The owner's goal:
express runs as **graphs** (configurations, not code edits), prove the
container works bit-identically over the existing engine, and only then
improve the optimization itself.

The current shape, expressed as the v1 graph (verified against the code and
`test/golden/baseline.json`):

```
jtml-production:  [Trunk: classic DIRECT, budget 20000, range (35)^6, dil 6]
               -> [Branch x2: classic DIRECT, budget 5000 each, range (15,15,25,25,25,25), dil 4]
               -> [Leaf: classic DIRECT, budget 5000, range (3,3,15,3,3,3), dil 1]
cumulative caps: 20000 / 25000 / 30000 / 35000
```

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1 (graph = ordered stages, implicit seed-forwarding edges): U7, U9
- R2 (C++-typed named registry; manifest references by name): U7
- R3 (per-stage optimizer-variant slot, bit-identical classic default): U8
- R4 (execute through existing seams; no new layer; Cut E deferred): U7, U9
- R5 (schema must not preclude biplane / tiered-dilation / polish): U7
- R6 (v1 registry ships `jtml-production`; stubs allowed): U7, U9

## Key Technical Decisions

- **StageScript as pure functions in a dedicated TU**
  (`include/coordinator/optimizer_stage_script.h` + `src/coordinator/optimizer_stage_script.cpp`):
  `StageSpec {StageKind kind, Point6D range, unsigned int budget, unsigned
  int repeat, unsigned int cfm_index}` + `BuildStageScript` +
  `DeriveStageCostParams` — one added line in `jtml_coordinator`'s explicit
  source list. Mirrors the run's angle-04 sketch; verified 1:1 against the
  current loop blocks (trunk `{Trunk, (35)^6, 20000, 1, 0}`, branch group
  `{Branch, branch_range, 5000, number_branches, 1}`, leaf `{Leaf, (3,3,15,3,3,3), 5000, 1, 2}`,
  Sym_Trap `{Leaf, ..., 0, 2}` for repeat=0).
- **`DeriveStageCostParams` reproduces the manager's parameter scan**
  (optimizer_manager.cpp:237–345) — NOT the CFM internals: dilation stays
  cost-owned, and the wizard "DO NOT EDIT" regions in `CostFunctionManager.*`
  are never touched by the derivation (the stage-guard bug fix at
  CostFunctionManager.cpp:46–48 is the one in-place exception, one line,
  flagged with a comment).
- **`BuildGpuCostAdapter` carries `Calibration` by value** (monoplane
  default) — closes the oracle-twin's monoplane-only gap and serves the
  future biplane consumer without a signature change.
- **`DirectOptimizer::Options` via guarded divergence**: every new path
  guards on "different from default" so defaults reproduce today's search
  bit-identically (R13); the launch plumbing (OptimizerRunLaunch → adapter →
  Initialize → RunDirectStage) is additive only.
- **The stage-guard bug is fixed in place** (tautology `||` → `&&`): the
  CFM's `stage_` is not the stage source of truth going forward — the
  StageScript `cfm_index` is — so no accessor relocation into wizard-owned
  regions.
- **One re-baseline, single-variable**: distance-map index fix only; Canny
  pinned 3/0/150; recovered-pose delta recorded explicitly; no other change
  bundled (origin Finding 12).
- **Convergence-tradeoff design note lives in the stage-script TU**: cover is
  a stage-loop property, intentionally dropped across stages (Flood L447–458);
  `Options` carries NO cover knob.

Today's Optimize() (verified landmarks)          After Cut B (script-driven)
------------------------------------------------  -------------------------------------------------

  dilate + emit UpdateDilationBackground              init CFM s.cfm_index + DeriveStageCostParams

15:Round 3 (wave 1) moved the run's evidentiary base onto the primary texts (angles 01–04 re-verified against the Zotero corpus) and resolved three open contradictions outright: (1) **Mahfouz normalization** — the paper corroborates the kernel's structure (two predicted-sum-normalized ratios, contour weighted more heavily, negative weights, a 3-px capture band — a full lineage match) but the numeric weights are unextractable (embedded PDF equations), so the kernel-as-spec verdict keeps 2.55/×255/−2.67/−1 and only the pointer-guard fix proceeds; (2) **three-way dilation contradiction** — Flood's constants are verbatim (femur 10/6/1, tibia 6/2/1, branch = trunk−4, leaf = 1); leaf=1 is unanimous, trunk 6 is the paper's TIBIA value applied to a FEMUR (femur robust band 8–12), and BOTH 6/4/1 and 6/3/1 violate branch=trunk−4 — the dilation-schedule ablation now tests the lineage configs {10,6,1}, {6,2,1}, {6,4,1}, {6,3,1} plus a bilateral-vs-render-only semantics axis; (3) **GLh formula** — verified from the paper itself (raw surrogate f_min + d stored, selection-time normalized d̃ = d/√n with f̃_min ≡ 0, f̃=1 flat case, 1e-6 recompute threshold, Definition-1 feasibility detection) with a ready-made constrained battery (Emmental-GKLS, 100/100 solved by GLh in the paper).
49:- z-profile probe executable: entry points verified (RunDirectStage lambda optimizer_manager.cpp:1235-1246; public twin EvaluateCostFunctionAtPoint :1372-1387; oracle twin oracle_test.cpp:286-291); 31-render Δz sweep; metrics valley_depth / argmin_offset / plateau_halfwidth / noise_floor; assertions p1–p4 (min-at-zero within noise; valley_depth<0.05 ⇒ z-blind; ranking asserted pin-first — run 1 records, later runs enforce; z_gap anti-correlates with valley_depth); dilations {6,3,1,4} so the probe arbitrates the 6/3/1-vs-6/4/1 contradiction by data. Wave 2 (angle 06 R2-1) adds the term-decomposition mode to the same probe: record full/chamfer/dilated costs from the SAME render at each sweep point (zero extra renders) — the instrument that arbitrates the polish precondition G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org R2-1]
84:- Dilation 6/3/1-vs-6/4/1: still numerically open, but the z-profile probe at {6,3,1,4} + the ablation manifest now arbitrate it by data rather than docs. (02 R2, 03 R2-2)
111:- DILATION CONTRADICTION RESOLVED (three-way) against Flood 2018 (floodAutomatedRegistration3D2018.txt): every dispatch number verified verbatim — femur trunk 10 / tibia 6, "dilation was decreased by a value of four in the branch search stage, and the final z-search stage was conducted at a dilation level of one", budgets 50k/3×15k/50k, branch ranges 15/15/25/25/25/25, z-leaf 5/5/20/5/5/5, Canny aperture 3 with 40/120 (tibia + Group B) or 30/80 (femur A). Resolution: leaf=1 is UNANIMOUS (code, docs, paper); trunk 6 (code AND docs) equals the paper's TIBIA trunk while the oracle optimizes a FEMUR (paper femur robust band 8–12, Table V; tibia band 4–8); branch 4 (code) and 3 (docs) BOTH violate the paper's branch=trunk−4 rule (→ 2 for trunk 6, → 6 for femur trunk 10); the docs' 6/3/1 matches no rule at all. The dilation-schedule ablation now tests the LINEAGE configs {10,6,1}, {6,2,1}, {6,4,1}, {6,3,1} PLUS a bilateral-vs-render-only SEMANTICS axis (the paper is internally inconsistent: §II-B-3 contains both "the generated silhouette is dilated to a value of one" and "In this stage both comparison and input images have the same dilation level"; Fig. 4 uses same-dilation-both — the repo's "(DIFFERENT FROM JTA PAPER)" comment (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:69) is contradicted by the paper's own passages; the semantics axis matters because the z-plateau width is ~2×dilation for bilateral vs ~1× for render-only). The paper's size caveat ("ideal dilation values are likely to also depend on the size of the implant in pixels") legitimizes the ablation; the paper's 145k/3-branch shape is recorded as a lineage dimension (nightly-only arm). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org R3-2]
116:- Z-LEAF BUDGET first-class: Flood's z (leaf-equivalent) budget is 50,000 evals — EQUAL to the trunk (50k/3×15k/50k = 145k total, ~3,000 evals/s on a GTX 970, "50 seconds per frame") — over a 20 mm out-of-plane range vs 5 mm in-plane, explicitly "because it is the least accurate degree of freedom for single-plane fluoroscopy". JTML's z-fraction: 5k/35k = 14.3% vs Flood's 50k/145k = 34.5% — a 2.4× lower z-fraction against the run's load-bearing z-weak axis. Spec updates: (a) budget_shapes gains "flood-direct-jta" {trunk 50000, branch 15000, number_branches 3, leaf 50000} → cumulative caps [50000, 65000, 80000, 95000, 145000], which the stage-bookkeeping gate extends to naturally; (b) the z-stage budget becomes an explicit ablation axis z_leaf_budget ∈ {5000 (JTML prod), 20000 (JTML trunk parity), 50000 (Flood parity)} crossed with the z-range axis {15 mm, 20 mm} (budget and range separable); (c) the dilation axis gains the "flood-femur-10-6-1" and "flood-tibia-6-2-1" reference points. Flood's success metric (in-plane ≤ 1 mm, rotations ≤ 1°, z excluded) validates the banded-informational z-gate doctrine by the lineage's own measurement convention. Transferability caveat: Flood's metric is the GPU-cheap unnormalized L1 on edge images; JTML's per-eval cost is 50–150× slower — the transfer question is exactly what the per-stage Moré & Wild data profile measures. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R3-1]
122:- STAGESCRIPT FIDELITY verified against Flood's real staging: the Round-2 schema {kind, range, budget, repeat, cfm_index} expresses the lineage config term-for-term with ZERO schema extension — 3 branch restarts at the same dilation → repeat=3 (dilate+emit once, repeats re-seed only); asymmetric z-leaf (20 mm z vs 5 mm/deg) → Point6D(5,5,20,5,5,5); per-stage dilation → cfm_index + CFM parameter values (the paper's "decrement by 4, final 1" is a construction-time value policy, not a schema field); restart re-centered on the current minimum → per-repeat SetStartingPoint; the paper's stage taxonomy is exactly Trunk/Branch/Leaf. STRONGEST finding: JTML's settings_constants.h is a VERBATIM transcription of Flood's TIBIA configuration — TRUNK_DILATION=6 = "the tibia groups used a dilation level of 6"; BRANCH_RANGE (15,15,25,25,25,25) = the branch restart sizes exactly; APERTURE=3, thresholds 40/120, Z_SEARCH_DILATION=1 — the lineage IS the spec; the lineage-vs-today deltas (3→2 branches, 50k/15k×3/50k → 20k/5k×2/5k, leaf 20/5 → 15/3, dilation schedule) are ALL data deltas. Dilation triangulation gains a third point: paper rule (trunk−4) on tibia trunk 6 gives 6/2/1; BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE=2 implies 6−2=4 → 6/4/1 (the constant is vestigial — appears in no .cpp; the widgets first-run branch value is the literal 4, SettingsBridge.cpp:17-20); baseline.json records 6/3/1. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org R3-1]
124:- CUT B PIN STRATEGY vs the lineage: the golden pins ONLY the trunk member (flat shape (12,12,15,15,15,15), kBudget 3000 — a degenerate single-stage member of the lineage family, with no branch/leaf assertions at all); with Flood's staging as the target shape, the script-driven loop must preserve FOUR lineage invariants with assertion homes in the multi-stage oracle: (1) group-once dilation identical across all repeats (Flood: "Several branch restarts are performed, all at the same level of dilation") — the per-stage dilation manifest match IS the lineage assertion; (2) per-repeat re-seed from the current optimum (restart box "fixed around the location of the current function minimum") — assert the recovered-pose SEQUENCE (branch i's pose feeds branch i+1's seed), not just the final pose; (3) asymmetric z-leaf (z 20 ≫ 5; JTML preserves the asymmetry while tightening) — the leaf stage applies the asymmetric leaf range; (4) frame-to-frame seed chaining (Flood's automation claim: "subsequent frames can be automatically registered from the optimum pose in the previous image") — frame N's trunk seed == frame N−1's recovered optimum. Cut D moves only the twin's body; the factory must stay stage-shape-agnostic (no hard-coded range/budget/dilation inside). [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org R3-3]
130:- DILATION three-way contradiction: RESOLVED against Flood 2018 primary text — leaf=1 unanimous; trunk 6 = the paper's TIBIA value on a FEMUR (femur robust band 8–12, Table V); code 6/4/1 and docs 6/3/1 BOTH violate branch=trunk−4 (lineage gives 10/6/1 femur, 6/2/1 tibia); the dilation-schedule ablation now tests lineage configs {10,6,1},{6,2,1},{6,4,1},{6,3,1} + a bilateral-vs-render-only semantics axis. (02 R3-2, 04 R3-1)
154:- SANITY BASELINE verified verbatim (floodAutomatedRegistration3D2018.txt L568–574): the lineage ran 145,000 evals/frame (50k trunk + 3×15k branch + 50k z) at "approximately 3,000 iterations per second (50 seconds per frame)" on a 4 GHz i7-4790K + GTX 970 — arithmetic checks: 145,000/3,000 ≈ 48 s; "iteration" = cost-function eval; per-eval = 333 µs INCLUDING DIRECT host bookkeeping. Cost semantics (L157–162): the eval is "a simple L1 norm... can be computed by a graphics processing unit (GPU) extremely efficiently" — render + one L1 pass, NO chamfer/distance-map term, NO per-eval input dilation (the input Canny frame is dilated once per stage) — so JTML's extra metric stages (~7 kernels) are the workload delta vs Flood, not the render. Budget-by-time design (L568): "Iteration count for the algorithm was pegged to take approximately one minute of operating time" — the lineage sizes budgets by WALL TIME; JTML's are fixed eval counts (20k/5k×2/5k); a flag for the budget-constants conversation once evals/s rises. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R3-1]
199:- The ablation matrix must encode: 7 registered variants × budget shapes (production 20/25/30/35k, reduced CI shape, flat-3000 oracle shape, NEW "flood-direct-jta" 50k/15k×3/50k — nightly-only) × dilation schedules (now the LINEAGE set {6/4/1, 6/3/1, 10/6/1, 6/2/1} × bilateral-vs-render-only semantics) × Canny config {0/150, 40/120, 30/80} × backface ON/OFF × frames {0,1,2}. Cost profile: flat-3000 is "a few minutes" → ~20–60 evals/s → full 35k production shape ~10–30 min/frame → full matrix is hours, hence manifest-driven subsets: reduced shape per-PR, full shape nightly. Round 2: the reduced shape comes from a one-time Moré & Wild data-profile measurement (smallest cumulative budget with recovered IoU ≥ 0.98 on Kneel_1 frame 0), not another ad hoc number; the gpu ctest label is additive; the perturbation suite calibrates what the IoU 0.85 gate can and cannot see. Wave 2: Cut 0's per-eval timing record replaces the derived 20–60 evals/s estimate. Round 3: the lineage throughput datum (~3,000 evals/s on a 2018 GTX 970, Flood) is the strongest external anchor yet for that record — upgraded by wave 2 into a full falsifiable baseline (Finding 15) — and Flood's capture-range cliff (90% at 4 mm/4°, ~50% at 16 mm/16°) field-anchors the perturbation grid's Δ magnitudes. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "ablation runner", "CI integration" + R2-1/R2-4/R3-1/R3-4; angles/05-compute-perf.org, Cut 0 + R3-1/R3-3/R3-7; angles/04-backend-architecture.org R3-5]
